title: Run Responsive Video Source Selection on Media Change, Not Just On Load (Like Picture)

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The video element allows source elements to use media attributes to target various media conditions, and it has cross-browser support. That said, sources are only evaluated once, and not again after that, even if media conditions change. This can cause some confusion for developers who are used to the behavior of the picture element, but perhaps worse, it could lead to breakage in situations where a particular video aspect ratio is expected in a layout and the wrong format is displayed (Say, a portrait orientation video is targeted for small-screen layouts and a landscape video is meant for wider viewports, which is one way responsive video can be used).

It would be better if video could continue to evaluate sources whenever media changes after initial load. This would mean the time code of a video would need to be maintained in cases where a source swaps out.

As a sort of demo and proof of concept, [this article](https://scottjehl.com/posts/even-responsiver-video/) describes a lightweight web component implementation that instructs the browser to reevaluate its available sources when media conditions change, and it takes into account syncing the timecode when a source changes. 
- There's [a demo page that shows the behavior if you resize ](https://scottjehl.com/sandbox/video-media/reallyrwdvideo)
- And a repository for the code https://github.com/scottjehl/ResponsiveVideo
- Also [at the end of the article](https://scottjehl.com/posts/even-responsiver-video/), there's a first stab at a Web Platform Test function called `videoMediaChangeSupport` that the component itself uses before defining the custom element behavior. Perhaps it could be useful in a platform test.

It would be great to see this reassessment behavior built-into the way source elements are meant to be assessed and reassessed in the spec (and ultimately, natively in browsers).
